articles.summary: Most babies manage one 5-6 hour stretch by 3-4 months, with longer nights by 6-9 months. A pediatrician explains what's actually normal at every age.
articles.title: When Do Babies Sleep Through the Night? Age-by-Age Guide

articles.summary: Infant acid reflux is the everyday spit-up most babies do, and it is usually normal. Learn the difference between happy spitters and GERD, what causes reflux, how long it lasts, home feeding and positioning tips, and the warning signs that mean you should call your pediatrician.
articles.title: Infant Acid Reflux: A Pediatrician's Guide to Symptoms, Causes, and When to Worry
